statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail). Let k be the unique integer with 0 <= k <= n-1 such that bits[j] = 1 for every j with n-1-k <= j <= n-2, and either n-1-k = 0 or bits[n-2-k] = 0; this k is the length of the maximal contiguous suffix of 1s immediately before the final 0. Then r = true if and only if k is even. Equivalently, in the unique decomposition of the whole array into contiguous blocks each equal to [0], [1,0], or [1,1], r = true exactly when the final block is the one-bit block [0] at index n-1, and r = false exactly when the final block is the two-bit block [1,0] at indices n-2 and n-1.
preconditions: Let n = len(bits). 1 <= n <= 1000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, bits[i] is either 0 or 1. bits[n-1] = 0.
